calibration.source: the certified dataset pinned by the installed policyengine bundle: Microcosm UK from policyengine 6.10.1, policyengine-uk-data before it
calibration.vintage: as pinned by the installed bundle

forecast.vintage: OBR Economic and fiscal outlook, October 2026 (Annex A, Tables A.1 and A.3), applied over policyengine-uk's March 2026 growth rates by src/uk_budget_data/forecast/obr_october_2026.json

basis.notes: The forecast is rebased on the Budget's OBR forecast: every simulation, baseline and reform alike, is built on the October 2026 growth rates in src/uk_budget_data/forecast/obr_october_2026.json (CPI, RPI, average earnings, house prices; the September 2027 CPI gap). Series that file does not list keep the March 2026 path the installed policyengine-uk ships; the receipt records the exact model version.

domestic_electricity_zero_vat.description: VAT on domestic electricity is 0% instead of 5% from 1 October 2026 to 30 June 2027: in Great Britain to March 2027 and across the UK from April 2027. The model's baseline has no zero rate, so the measure covers the whole period, as the Treasury costs it. It applies to electricity spending only. 2026-27 carries the October to March share of a year's electricity use (about 57%), not a share of its days; 2027-28 its 91 days of 366.
domestic_electricity_zero_vat.name: Zero VAT on domestic electricity

fuel_duty_rise_deferral.description: The 5p cut in fuel duty is kept: the main rate stays at 52.95p a litre to 30 June 2027, so the rise due on 1 January 2027 and the March and April 2027 steps do not happen. From 1 July 2027 it returns to current law's 60.59p a litre, rising with RPI each April. Rates are day-weighted to fiscal years, and the VAT on the lower pump price is included.
fuel_duty_rise_deferral.name: Fuel duty cut extended

attestation.reason: PREVIEW ONLY — not a signature. Local preview placeholder; nobody has reviewed this receipt. Checked budget_measures.household_energy_payment_2026: in 2026-27 only it adds the payment to ebr_council_tax_rebate for households in England whose council tax band is A, B, C or D, leaving every other household and year at the native amount. The receipt's outputs were compared with the hand-computed households in tests/test_reforms.py.

household_energy_payment_2026.description: A one-off £100 payment from January 2027 to each household in England in property valuation bands A to D (the lowest four of England's eight), up to 20 million households, paid into bank accounts and counted as household income in 2026-27. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland receive a share of the funding instead, which is not modelled.
household_energy_payment_2026.name: Household Energy Payment

trading_allowance_raise.description: From 6 April 2027 the trading allowance, which relieves trading receipts in place of actual expenses, rises from £1,000 to £3,000, for income tax and Class 4 National Insurance. Without gross receipts in the data, a profit within the allowance is treated as fully relieved, so the cost may be overstated.
trading_allowance_raise.name: Trading allowance raised to £3,000

unearned_income_rates_up.description: From 6 April 2027 the income tax rates on savings income rise to 24%, 44% and 49% at the basic, higher and additional rates across the UK, and those on property income to the same rates in England, Wales and Northern Ireland: 2 percentage points above current law, which already includes Budget 2025's rises. Finance cost relief for landlords follows the property basic rate, so rises to 24%. Dividend rates are unchanged. Incomes are held fixed, with no behavioural response.
unearned_income_rates_up.name: Savings and property income tax rates up
